contractSource.method: live tools/list + tools/call + resources/read against the running FastMCP server

server.name: scrcpymac-phone-agent
server.instructions: Control a connected Android phone. The plugin owns its standalone scrcpy H.264 and control session; ScrcpyMac.app is not required. ADB remains available for screenshots and accessibility automation. For Chinese text, use phone_paste. WeChat: com.tencent.mm.
server.versionReported: the installed mcp SDK version (FastMCP passes no explicit version); Go should report the plugin version instead -- see mcp-contract.md

jsonResult.goEquivalent: encoding/json Encoder with SetIndent("", "  ") and SetEscapeHTML(false), minus the trailing newline
jsonResult.keyOrder: insertion order of the Python dict -- NOT alphabetical. Go must preserve it.

okWrapper.consequence: "ok" is APPENDED LAST when the action payload did not already carry it (phone_backend, phone_list_devices, phone_device_info, phone_screenshot, phone_current_app) and stays FIRST when it did (every actions.* payload).

errWrapper.note: Every phone_* tool except phone_doctor wraps its body in try/except (AdbError, OSError). The MCP-level isError stays FALSE; failure is carried in the JSON body only.

resource.name: scrcpymac-app
resource.title: ScrcpyMac
resource.description: Interactive Android mirroring and control workspace.
resource.missingFileError: ScrcpyMac widget build is missing. Run scripts/build-ui.sh.
resource.connectDomainsOrdering: connectDomains/connect_domains are computed ONCE at registration time by ScrcpyRuntime.stream_connect_domains(), which calls _ensure_loopback() and binds 127.0.0.1:0. register_scrcpymac_app runs at import of phone_agent.server (line 57), BEFORE any @mcp.tool decorator and long before any stream starts. The literal port baked into the CSP is therefore the loopback port allocated at process start. ScrcpyRuntime.close() nils _loopback, so a subsequent _ensure_loopback() would bind a DIFFERENT port while the resource _meta still advertises the old one. The wildcard entries (http://127.0.0.1:*, ws://127.0.0.1:* and the localhost variants) are what actually keep the widget working today -- a live suspect in the 1 FPS investigation.

tools.name: open_scrcpymac
tools.title: Open ScrcpyMac
tools.description: Open the complete ScrcpyMac phone workspace in Codex.
notes: display_mode is normalised: any value other than "inline" or "fullscreen" becomes "fullscreen".
widget is always the literal "scrcpymac-app"; phase is always the literal "standalone-h264-stream".
Cannot fail: there is no try/except and no device access.

tools.name: scrcpymac_ui_state
tools.title: Read ScrcpyMac UI state
tools.description: Return device discovery and backend state for the ScrcpyMac widget.
notes: IMPORTANT: on AdbError/OSError this tool returns isError=FALSE with ok=false, a populated "error" string, devices=[] and the full stream status. It does NOT use the _error() helper. The text block on that path is str(exc), not a sentence.
devices[] items are {serial,state,model,product}.
stream is the full ScrcpyRuntime.status() payload (see streamStatusKeys).

tools.name: scrcpymac_ui_select_device
tools.title: Select ScrcpyMac device
tools.description: Select the Android serial used by subsequent widget actions.
notes: device is the matching {serial,state,model,product} entry from adb devices -l.
Errors: empty serial -> "device serial must not be empty"; unknown serial -> "Android device not found: {serial}"; wrong state -> "Android device is {state}: {serial}".

tools.name: scrcpymac_ui_start_stream
tools.title: Start standalone ScrcpyMac stream
tools.description: Start the plugin-owned scrcpy H.264 and control session.
tools.textBlock: Started the standalone ScrcpyMac H.264 stream.
notes: Selects the device first (actions.select_device(serial)), then runtime.start().
max_fps is snapped: >=45 -> 60, otherwise 30. resolution_percent is clamped to [25,100].
Returns ScrcpyRuntime.status() taken immediately after the video thread starts.

tools.name: scrcpymac_ui_stream_status
tools.title: Read standalone ScrcpyMac stream status
tools.description: Read the plugin-owned H.264 stream state and measured FPS.
tools.textBlock: Read the standalone ScrcpyMac stream status.
notes: No try/except: this tool cannot return isError.

The 7 base keys are always present. serial/deviceName/deviceWidth/deviceHeight/frameWidth/frameHeight/maxFps/resolutionPercent/codec are added only while _meta is set. streamUrl is added only when state=="streaming" AND a loopback port AND a token exist.

tools.name: scrcpymac_ui_stop_stream
tools.title: Stop standalone ScrcpyMac stream
tools.description: Stop the plugin-owned scrcpy session and release its adb forward.
notes: runtime.stop() clears _meta on a clean stop, so the device/frame keys disappear; after an error stop the state is "error", _meta is retained and those keys remain.

tools.name: scrcpymac_ui_snapshot
tools.title: Capture ScrcpyMac preview frame
tools.description: Capture a compressed frame for the ScrcpyMac widget.
notes: max_width clamped to [320,1200]; quality clamped to [45,90] BEFORE use.

PhoneActions.preview_frame ignores both arguments and returns a full adb screencap PNG; _preview_frame then downscales to max_width (BILINEAR, only if wider) and re-encodes JPEG at the clamped quality with optimize=False. mimeType is then "image/jpeg".
If the shot dict carries "image_bytes" (a future H.264-derived path) the bytes are passed through untouched and mimeType comes from shot["mime_type"] defaulting to "image/jpeg".
The base64 payload appears ONLY in structuredContent.dataBase64, never in the text block.

tools.name: scrcpymac_ui_tap
tools.title: Tap ScrcpyMac preview
tools.description: Tap normalized preview coordinates.
notes: Two different payload shapes. When runtime.is_active(): runtime.tap_relative() -> {ok,action,serial,point,coordinateSpace,backend} with backend="plugin-control". Otherwise actions.tap_relative(x,y,verify=False,retries=0) -> {ok,coordinate_space,source,device_point,tap}.
Runtime path clamps x/y to [0,1]. adb path REJECTS out-of-range with "relative x and y must be between 0 and 1".

tools.name: scrcpymac_ui_swipe
tools.title: Swipe ScrcpyMac preview
tools.description: Swipe between normalized preview coordinates.
notes: All four coordinates are validated 0<=v<=1 first -> AdbError "swipe coordinates must be between 0 and 1".
duration_ms clamped to [0,10000].

Runtime path -> camelCase durationMs, backend="plugin-control". adb fallback -> snake_case duration_ms, no backend key; it converts to device pixels via round(v*(size-1)) using device_info()["screen"].
The except clause also catches KeyError/TypeError/ValueError.

tools.name: scrcpymac_ui_key
tools.title: Press ScrcpyMac navigation key
tools.description: Press an Android navigation or hardware key.
notes: Runtime path (runtime.key) supports back,home,recents,enter,delete,tab,menu,power,volume_up,volume_down -- NOT "paste". adb path (actions.key) supports the same set PLUS "paste" (keycode 279).
Unknown key error text differs by path: ScrcpyRuntimeError/AdbError "Unknown key {name!r}. Supported: <comma-separated list>" where the list is the runtime's 10 keys or actions' 11 keys respectively.

tools.name: scrcpymac_ui_paste
tools.title: Paste text through ScrcpyMac
tools.description: Paste text into the focused Android field.
notes: length is len(text) in Unicode code points (Python), NOT bytes. Go must count runes.
Empty text -> error "text must not be empty".

tools.name: scrcpymac_ui_connect_wifi
tools.title: Connect ScrcpyMac over Wi-Fi
tools.description: Connect adb to an Android device over Wi-Fi.
notes: host is .strip()ped before use. target = host if it already contains ':' else f"{host}:{port}".
output is the trimmed stdout of `adb connect <target>`.

tools.name: phone_backend
tools.description: Report whether the standalone H.264 runtime or adb fallback is active.
notes: backend is "plugin-h264" while streaming, otherwise "adb".

tools.name: phone_doctor
tools.description: Run environment diagnostics (adb, device, ScrcpyMac Agent, Python dependencies).
notes: NOT wrapped by _ok/_err: it is json_result(run_doctor()) directly, so "ok" is FIRST here.
Early return when adb cannot be resolved: only {ok:false, version, checks, summary:"adb is required before controlling a phone"} -- no backend, no uv_available.
checks[] items are {name, ok, detail} plus optional extras: scrcpy_server/adb add "bundled" (bool), device adds "devices" (list), foreground_app adds "activity".

Check names in order: platform, python, mcp_package, scrcpy_server, adb, adb_version, device, then screen_size + foreground_app only when exactly one device is ready, then runtime_architecture (which also carries backend="plugin-h264").
backend = "plugin-h264-ready" when scrcpy-server resolved, else "adb".
ok = all checks ok EXCLUDING the foreground_app check.
version is phone_agent.__version__ (currently "0.7.2").
No try/except: an unexpected exception surfaces as a real isError=true result.

tools.name: phone_list_devices
tools.description: List Android devices visible to adb.
notes: devices[] items are {serial,state,model,product}; model/product default to "".

tools.name: phone_device_info
tools.description: Get connected device serial, screen size, and foreground app.
notes: While streaming: backend="plugin-h264", screen={width,height} from the native size, and an extra video={width,height,fps,codec}.
Otherwise: backend="adb", screen={width,height} from `wm size`, no video key.
foreground is always {package,activity,raw}.

tools.name: phone_screenshot
tools.description: Capture the device screen. Returns metadata JSON and optionally a PNG image.
notes: The ONLY tool in server.py with no return annotation, so FastMCP emits NO outputSchema and structuredContent is null on every path.
include_image=true -> content = [TextContent(json without base64), ImageContent(png)]. The ImageContent is {type:"image", data:<base64 png>, mimeType:"image/png"}.
include_image=false -> content = [TextContent(json WITH a "base64" key)] only.
format is always the literal "png"; size_bytes is len(png).
On AdbError/OSError only a single TextContent with {"ok":false,"error":...} is emitted (no image block), still isError=false.

tools.name: phone_tap
tools.description: Tap native device pixels. By default verifies a screen change and retries nearby.
notes: x/y are clamped to the device screen before tapping (max(0,min(size-1,v))).
Streaming path uses runtime.tap_relative(x/(w-1), y/(h-1)) and returns the plugin-control shape {ok,action,serial,point,coordinateSpace,backend}. adb path returns {ok,action,x,y,serial}.
verify=true adds a "verification" object to whichever shape came back:
* baseline screenshot failed -> {requested:true, available:false, attempts:1} and 1 tap.
* verified -> {requested:true, available:true, verified:true, attempts:[...], after_size_bytes:int}.
* not verified -> {requested:true, available:true, verified:false, attempts:[...], hint:"No screen change detected after tapping the target and nearby points."}.
attempts[] items are {point:[x,y], screen_changed:bool, change_score:float(4dp)}.

retries is clamped to [0,4] and selects the first retries+1 offsets from [(0,0),(0,-32),(0,32),(-32,0),(32,0)]; settle 0.45s between taps; change threshold 0.035 on a 72x128 RGB resample with per-pixel max-channel delta >= 20.

tools.name: phone_tap_relative
tools.description: Tap normalized screenshot coordinates where x and y are between 0 and 1.
notes: coordinate_space is always the literal "relative"; source is [x,y] as given; device_point is [round(x*(w-1)), round(y*(h-1))].
tap is the nested phone_tap payload (including its verification object).
Out of range -> AdbError "relative x and y must be between 0 and 1".
Python's round() is banker's rounding (round-half-to-even). Go's math.Round is not.

tools.name: phone_tap_image
tools.description:
Tap a point measured on a displayed/resized screenshot.

Pass the exact width and height of the image coordinate space used to
choose x/y. The tool maps it into current native device pixels.
notes: coordinate_space is always the literal "image"; source is {point:[x,y], size:[image_width,image_height]}; device_size is [w,h].
device_point = [round(x/max(iw-1,1)*(w-1)), round(y/max(ih-1,1)*(h-1))].
Errors: non-positive size -> "image_width and image_height must be positive"; point outside -> "image point must be inside image_width x image_height".

tools.name: phone_swipe
tools.description: Swipe from (x1,y1) to (x2,y2).
notes: adb path -> snake_case duration_ms and no backend key. Streaming path -> runtime.swipe_relative -> camelCase durationMs plus backend="plugin-control", and from/to are in FRAME coordinates (meta.width/height), not device pixels.

tools.name: phone_long_press
tools.description: Long press at coordinates.
notes: Implemented as swipe(x,y,x,y,duration_ms) -> action is "swipe", NOT "long_press".

tools.name: phone_key
tools.description: Press a key: back, home, recents, enter, delete, tab, menu, power, paste.
notes: key is name.lower().strip(). Supported (adb path): back=4, home=3, recents=187, enter=66, delete=67, tab=61, menu=82, power=26, volume_up=24, volume_down=25, paste=279.
The streaming path drops "paste" and returns {ok,action,key,serial,backend} with NO code.
Unknown key error: "Unknown key {name!r}. Supported: back, home, recents, enter, delete, tab, menu, power, volume_up, volume_down, paste" -- note Python !r quoting (single quotes).
Note the docstring only advertises 9 of the 11 keys (volume_up/volume_down are undocumented but accepted).

tools.name: phone_type
tools.description: Type short ASCII text. Do not use for Chinese — use phone_paste instead.
notes: Always the adb path, even while streaming.
Escaping: text.replace("%","%25").replace(" ","%s") then shlex.quote for the device shell.
length is the rune count of the ORIGINAL text.
Empty text -> "text must not be empty".

tools.name: phone_paste
tools.description: Paste text via device clipboard (supports Chinese and emoji).
notes: adb path: `cmd clipboard set-text <quoted>`, sleep 150ms, `input keyevent 279`.
Streaming path: scrcpy control message type 9 (set clipboard, paste=1) -> adds backend="plugin-control".

tools.name: phone_launch_app
tools.description: Launch an Android app by package name. Example WeChat: com.tencent.mm.
notes: activity is JSON null when the empty-string default was used (server.py passes activity or None).
With activity: `am start -n pkg/activity`. Without: `monkey -p pkg -c android.intent.category.LAUNCHER 1`. Then sleeps 1.0s before reading the foreground app.
action is always the literal "launch".

tools.name: phone_current_app
tools.description: Get the foreground app package and activity.
notes: foreground is {package,activity,raw}; raw is the trimmed dumpsys line.

tools.name: phone_ui_tree
tools.description:
Dump the UI accessibility tree as JSON nodes or raw XML.
Nodes carry state flags (scrollable, enabled=false, focused, checked...)
only when noteworthy. If the result has "degraded": true, the tree is
incomplete (WebView/Compose/game) — call phone_screenshot and use vision
instead.
notes: compact=true -> {ok,nodes,count,serial} plus optional degraded+hint. compact=false -> {ok,xml,serial}.

Node object key order: index, text, content_desc, resource_id, class, clickable, bounds, center. Then, ONLY when noteworthy: scrollable(true), enabled(false), password(true), focused(true), selected(true), checkable(true)+checked(bool).
center is [x,y] parsed from bounds "[x1,y1][x2,y2]" with integer floor division, or null.
A node is kept only if it has text, content-desc, clickable, scrollable, "EditText" in class, or checkable.

degraded=true + hint "UI tree looks incomplete (WebView/Compose/custom-drawn). Fall back to phone_screenshot for vision." when any class contains WebView OR fewer than 3 nodes are clickable-or-texted.
XML parse failure -> {ok:true, xml, serial, parse_error:true, degraded:true, hint:"UI dump was empty or unparseable. Retry phone_ui_tree or fall back to phone_screenshot for vision."}.
An empty dump is retried once after 300ms.
Results are cached per PhoneActions instance and invalidated by every tap/swipe/key/type/paste/launch/select_device.

tools.name: phone_find_and_tap
tools.description:
Find a UI element by visible text, content-desc, resource-id, or class,
then tap it. Provide at least one selector. require_all=True demands every
given selector to hit (use text + resource_id to disambiguate); exact=True
matches whole strings instead of substrings; index=N picks the Nth match;
scroll_to_find=N scrolls down up to N times when the element is off-screen.
notes: matched is the compact ui_tree node; tap is the nested phone_tap payload.
No selector at all -> "Provide text, content_desc, resource_id, or class_name".
Timeout -> "Element not found within {timeout_s}s ({criteria}). Last tree had {n} nodes[, after {k} scroll(s)]." The criteria rendering uses Python repr of a list of strings.
Matched node without bounds -> "Matched node has no tappable bounds ({criteria})".
Matching: substring by default, whole-string with exact=true; ANY specified attribute hits unless require_all=true; disabled nodes are skipped; index picks the Nth match.
Polling: 0.4s base interval with 1.5^n backoff capped at 2.0s; a scroll (mid-screen swipe 70%->30% over 350ms + 0.4s settle) re-dumps immediately with no backoff.

tools.name: phone_wait_for_text
tools.description: Wait until the given text appears in the UI tree.
notes: found is the compact ui_tree node. serial falls back to the client serial when the tree carries none.
Matches by substring on the text attribute only.

tools.name: phone_shell
tools.description: Execute an adb shell command on the device.
notes: output is the trimmed stdout of `adb shell <command>`; 60s timeout.

tools.name: phone_send_wechat
tools.description: High-level recipe: open WeChat, find a contact, and send a message.
notes: recipe is always the literal "wechat_send_message".
verification is {width,height,size_bytes} from a final screenshot.

steps[] entries are heterogeneous: {step,result} for launch_wechat/wait_wechat_ready/open_search/wait_search_input/open_chat/tap_send; {step,contact} for type_contact; {step,length} for type_message; {step,key} for open_chat_fallback/send_fallback; {step,skipped} for the skipped waits.
Failure message is rewritten: "{exc}. Steps completed: {n}. Last screenshot: {w}x{h}".

tools.name: phone_enable_wifi_adb
tools.description: Enable TCP/IP adb on a USB-connected device (required before Wi-Fi connect).
notes: action is always "enable_tcpip"; output is the trimmed `adb shell tcpip <port>` stdout.

tools.name: phone_get_device_ip
tools.description: Get the device's Wi-Fi IP address (for wireless adb).
notes: Tries `ip route | awk '/wlan/ {print $9; exit}'` then `ip -f inet addr show wlan0 ... | cut -d/ -f1`; both must match ^\d+\.\d+\.\d+\.\d+$.
Failure -> "Could not detect device Wi-Fi IP. Is Wi-Fi connected?"

tools.name: phone_connect_wifi
tools.description: Connect to a device over Wi-Fi adb. Example host: 192.168.1.100.
notes: action is always "connect_wifi"; target = host if it contains ':' else f"{host}:{port}".
NOTE: unlike scrcpymac_ui_connect_wifi, host is NOT stripped here.
Uses self.client (no ensure_device), so it works with no device attached.

tools.name: phone_disconnect_wifi
tools.description: Disconnect a Wi-Fi adb session. Leave host empty to disconnect all.
notes: action is always "disconnect_wifi". Empty host -> `adb disconnect` (all). Non-empty host without ':' gets ":5555" appended REGARDLESS of any port argument (this tool has no port parameter).
